clue.text: A foot of water in the bishop's seat

indicators.note: in places the water term inside the word for the bishop's seat

parts.note: a bishop's seat is his see, the diocese
a pond is a small body of water

explanation.surface: Someone measures a foot of floodwater inside the cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A foot' is a metrical foot in verse, not a measure of depth.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody a foot of two stressed syllables has this name.

clue.text: Heels concealed by the proverbial 'cloaks.

explanation.surface: Shoes are hidden under capes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the dagger of 'cloak and dagger'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin high heels on women's shoes, and slim daggers hidden by the cloaks of cloak-and-dagger stories.

clue.text: Emergence of rock brings démodé hair style

parts.note: démodé means out of fashion, out
a crop is a short haircut

explanation.surface: Rock music's arrival makes a hair style old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrock showing at the surface of the ground is rock emerging.

clue.text: To put. it mildly what string does with H. King

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, king of Hades
one who strings along with another goes along with them

explanation.surface: Someone tactfully describes a violin string out of tune with a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'H. King' is the Hades king, Dis; 'string along with' means go along with, agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying two people differ is the mild way of saying they quarrel.

clue.text: Oriental divine 'has a book of legends

parts.note: E is short for east, the Orient
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Eastern holy man owns a volume of myths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' is a noun here, a clergyman, abbreviated by his degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Icelandic collection of Norse myths and poems.

clue.text: Between extremities, a river keeps going

indicators.note: between puts the river's name inside the word for extremities

parts.note: the extremities of something are its ends
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A river flows on between its far banks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: To last or persist is to keep going.

clue.text: When a Shropshire lad's Cherry wore white?

definitions.text: When a Shropshire lad's Cherry wore white?

parts.words: When a Shropshire lad's Cherry wore white?
parts.note: Housman's A Shropshire Lad has the cherry tree 'wearing white' for the spring church season

explanation.surface: A country boy's girlfriend wears white on some occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cherry' looks like a girl's name; it is the tree in Housman's 'Loveliest of trees', 'wearing white' for the spring festival.
explanation.definitionFit: The cherry blossoms white during the church season following the Resurrection.

clue.text: Funny guy's girl? That's about right

indicators.note: about places the girl's word around the abbreviation

parts.note: doll is old slang for a girl

explanation.surface: A comic asks if his girlfriend is right for him.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a jester or buffoon.

clue.text: Dish for an 'artist, a music-maker and myself.

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a viol is an old stringed instrument
I is the speaker, myself

explanation.surface: A meal is ordered for a painter, a musician and the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian pasta parcels served as a course.

clue.text: Many in the team move furtively

indicators.note: in places the Roman numeral inside the word for team

parts.note: a side is a team
L is fifty in Roman numerals, so many

explanation.surface: Lots of players on the team creep about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives a large Roman numeral, L.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge along sideways and stealthily is to creep.

clue.text: Stroke is cut badly

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A stroke play shot is mishit and cut badly.
explanation.definitionFit: In verse, the stressed beat of a line is called this, a metrical stroke or accent.

clue.text: Like Tudor monasteries in -hot water ?

explanation.surface: Henry VIII's monasteries got into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In hot water' looks like 'in trouble', but sugar put in hot water melts away.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII closed down the monasteries, the Dissolution; a solid stirred into hot water melts and disperses.

clue.text: Note, anger can be more than anger

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: can be signals that the word anger may be rearranged into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A remark that annoyance can grow beyond plain annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' turns ANGER into NRAGE; 'anger' at the end is a verb, and to do more than anger someone is to make them furious.
explanation.definitionFit: To infuriate is to go further than merely annoying someone.

clue.text: Bravo ! But it's not rare

explanation.surface: Someone cheers a steak and notes it is cooked through.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of congratulation, and a steak cooked right through rather than bloody.

clue.text: Still: short of a proposal

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put to a meeting
less means without, short of

explanation.surface: Something is not quite a formal motion.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse order: 'short of a proposal' is motion-less.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmoving means not moving at all.

clue.text: Protection from the sun given by physical education, in extremity

indicators.note: in places the school-subject abbreviation inside the extremity

parts.note: a toe is an extremity of the body

explanation.surface: A school sports lesson supplies sunshade at the extreme.
explanation.walkthrough: A topee is the pith helmet worn in the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: A pith helmet worn to shield the head from tropical sun.

clue.text: Surpasses Salome on the dance floor?

explanation.surface: Salome outdoes everyone in her famous dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Salome's dance of the seven veils was a striptease: read the answer as 'out strips'.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass is to outdo or leave behind; Salome peeling off veils as she dances takes her clothes off.

clue.text: Cistercians sworn to keep the opening shut

definitions.text: sworn to keep the opening shut

explanation.surface: Monks are under oath to keep a door closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the opening' is the mouth, a 'trap' in slang: these monks keep silence.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict order of Cistercian monks, and men vowed to silence who keep their mouths shut.

clue.text: Terrible scenes about ten punishments

indicators.note: about places the rearranged letters around the number
terrible signals that the word scenes is wrecked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Awful scenes follow ten penalties being handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a container signal here, not 'concerning': the jumbled scenes go round the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Judges pass these penalties on the guilty.

clue.text: "He is well paid that is well —" (Mer. of Venice)

definitions.text: "He is well paid that is well —" (Mer. of Venice)

parts.words: "He is well paid that is well —" (Mer. of Venice)
parts.note: a line from Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice with its last word missing; the solver supplies it

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: Portia says this in Act IV of The Merchant of Venice, refusing payment after the trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Portia means that contentment is reward enough: one who is content is well paid.

clue.text: They provide support for those making exposures

definitions.text: They provide support for those making exposures

parts.words: They provide support for those making exposures
parts.note: exposures are photographs, not scandals: the stands that hold a camera steady

explanation.surface: Some people back whistleblowers revealing secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposures' looks like revelations of scandal, but means camera exposures.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-legged camera stands hold a camera steady for photographers.

clue.text: Pale as a White Leghorn — or less so?

parts.note: taken as written
the White Leghorn is a breed of hen

explanation.surface: Someone is as white as a white chicken, or not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or less so?' notes that ashen is a greyish pallor, a shade less than the hen's pure white.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey-faced from shock or illness is pale.

clue.text: Poet gets round doctor to give something stimulating

indicators.note: gets round places the poet's name around the doctor's abbreviation

parts.note: R. H. Horne was a Victorian poet
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A poet calls on his doctor for a tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Hengist Horne wrote the epic Orion.
explanation.definitionFit: A gland's chemical messenger stimulates activity in the body.

clue.text: Being niggardly one's duty with, gin cocktail

parts.note: a stint is a spell of allotted work, one's duty

indicators.note: cocktail signals that the word gin is mixed up

explanation.surface: A mean host serves only one gin cocktail while on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' mixes GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy or mean with money is niggardly.

clue.text: Macbeth's victim

parts.note: not Duncan: Macbeth hears a voice cry that he 'does murder' this

explanation.surface: Who did Macbeth kill?
explanation.walkthrough: Duncan is the first thought; Macbeth 'does murder sleep', and so cannot rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Macbeth murders rest itself along with the king.

clue.text: Detail the men for the subject

indicators.note: de-tail: remove the last letter of the words that follow

parts.note: taken as written; the run sits in these words only because the cut leaves all but the last letter, a coincidence of the deletion, not a hiding

explanation.surface: Officers assign some men to a task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detail' reads as de-tail, removing the N at the end of THEMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The topic of a talk or essay is its subject.

clue.text: Plant ruined by paying :guest, sure !

indicators.note: ruined signals that the letters given are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: PG is short for paying guest, a lodger

explanation.surface: A lodger insists something has been spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' scrambles PG and SURE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A family of plants with milky sap, the euphorbias.

clue.text: High French resort in America

parts.note: haut is French for high

explanation.surface: An upmarket French holiday spot in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as re-sort, rearranging HAUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of the American West, a place in America.

clue.text: Running away from work in water, for example

indicators.note: in places the word for work inside the classical element

parts.note: water is one of the four classical elements
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone flees from labour in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water, for example' gives the category, ELEMENT, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who run off to marry secretly make an escape.

clue.text: Philosopher helps in bringing chess to Iceland

indicators.note: the three words after help to carry the letters, spanning the word joins

explanation.surface: A thinker assists in taking chess to Iceland, home of a famous championship.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in 'chesS TO ICeland'.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Zeno's school, which taught calm endurance of hardship.

clue.text: Have the police, party gone. to the ship?

parts.note: a posse is a band of men gathered by a sheriff
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A question whether the police search party has boarded the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To own or hold something is to have it.

clue.text: Street, with holes, perhaps, .outside the: lodgings

indicators.note: outside places the rearranged letters around the street abbreviation
perhaps signals that the word holes may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A potholed street stands outside the boarding house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holes' is anagram fodder, not a description of a bumpy road; 'outside the' wraps the shuffle round the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap hostel accommodation is a form of lodgings.
